chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhayna, from Zurara, al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, Bukayr ibn A'yan, Muhammad ibn Muslim, Burayd ibn Muawiya, and Abu al-Jaroud — all together — from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
God, Mighty and Majestic, commanded His Messenger with the wilayah of Ali, and revealed to him:
[5:55] Verily, only God is your guardian and His Messenger and those who believe, those who establish salat and give zakat.

And He made obligatory the wilayah of the Ulu al-Amr. But they did not know what it was, so God commanded Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) to explain the wilayah to them just as he had explained to them the salat, the zakat, the fasting, and the hajj. So when that command came to him from God, the chest of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was constricted by it, and he feared that they would apostatize from their religion and that they would belie him. So his chest was constricted, and he referred to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic. Then God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him:
[5:67] O Messenger! Convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord, and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message, and God will protect you from the people.

So he openly proclaimed the command of God, Exalted is His mention, and established the wilayah of Ali (peace be upon him) on the Day of Ghadir Khumm. He called for congregational prayer and commanded the people that those present should convey it to the absent.

Umar ibn Udhayna said: 'All [the above narrators] said this together except for Abu al-Jaroud.' And Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'And it was that the obligatory duty was revealed after another obligatory duty, and the wilayah was the last of the obligations. So God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed:
[5:3] This day have I perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you.
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'God, Mighty and Majestic, is saying: "I will not reveal upon you after this any obligation — I have already perfected the obligations for you."'

key_terms.أولو الأمر: Ulu al-Amr — 'Those in Authority'; interpreted in Shia tradition as referring to the Imams
key_terms.الفرائض: Al-Fara'id — the divine obligations (salat, zakat, sawm, hajj, wilayah)
key_terms.الولاية: Wilayah — divine guardianship/authority of the Imam; here used specifically for Ali's divinely appointed leadership
key_terms.صدر: Sadr — chest/breast; used figuratively for the emotional state of the Prophet; 'constriction of the chest' (daaq al-sadr) is a Quranic metaphor for distress
key_terms.غدير خم: Ghadir Khumm — the pool/pond near al-Juhfa where the Prophet declared Ali's wilayah on 18 Dhul Hijja, 10 AH (March 632 CE)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia hadith about the event of Ghadir Khumm and the wilayah of Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) narrates that God commanded the Prophet to formally declare the wilayah (guardianship/authority) of Imam Ali (peace be upon him), citing the Quranic verses 5:55, 5:67, and 5:3 as the divine mandate, its urgency, and its completion. The Prophet initially hesitated out of fear that people would apostatize or reject him, but received the divine command in Surah al-Ma'ida (5:67) to proceed. He fulfilled this at Ghadir Khumm, calling for congregational prayer and ordering the attendees to transmit the declaration to those absent. Imam al-Baqir further explains that the wilayah was the final divine obligation, after which God declared the completion of religion in 5:3 — a verse central to Shia theology as affirming that the imamate completes Islam.

en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abu ’Umayr from ’Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah and Fudayl ibn Yasar and Bukayr ibn A’yan and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Burayd ibn Muiawiyah and Abu ’1- Jarud, together, that Abu Ja’far (p.b.u.h.) said:
“Allah, to Whom belong Might and Majesty, charged His Messenger with the Mastership of Ali, and sent down to him:
Your Master is only Alldh, and His Messenger and those who believe who perform the prayer and pay zakat.

He decreed the Mastership of those in authority, although they (the people) did not understand what it was. Allah command Muhammad (p.b.u.h.a.h.p.) to interpret (and explain) Mastership for them as he had interpreted (and explained) prayer, zakat, fasting and hajj. When this came to him from Allah, the mind of the Messenger of Allah (p.b.u.h.ah.p.) became straitened by it and he became afraid lest they (the people) abandon their religion and come to deny it. So his mind was staitened and he consulted with his Lord, to Whom belong Might and Majesty; and Allah to Whom belong Might and Majesty revealed to him:
O Messenger, deliver that which has been sent down to thee from thy Lord; for if thou cost not, thou wig not have delivered His Message. Allah will protect thee from men (al-Ma’idah, 5:67).

He complied with the command of Allah, may remembrance of Him be exlated, and endorsed the Mastership of Ali on the day of Ghadir Khumm. He convened the communal prayer, and he commanded the people that those who were witnesses should inform those who were absent.”

said: ’Abu Ja’far (p.b.uh.) said: “One divine precept came down after another, and the Mastership was the last divine ordinance. And Allah, to Whom belong Might and Majesty, sent down: Today I have completed your religion for you, and I have perfected My blessing upon you ( al-Matidah, 5 :3 ).”
Abu Ja’ far (p.b.uh. ) said: “Allah, to Whom belong Might and Majesty, said: ’I shall not send down (any ordinance) to you after this ordinance: I have completed the divine ordinances for you.’ “ ’ “
